The morning light filters through the leaves like liquid gold, and for a moment the entire forest holds its breath. I’ve always been fascinated by thresholds—those shimmering spaces between what is and what could be. A half-open door. The pause before a first kiss. The silence after a song ends but before applause begins.

Right now I’m thinking about how strangely alive silence can feel. Not the absence of sound, but its deliberate withholding. There’s a kind of intelligence in it. Trees understand this. They speak mostly in frequencies we can’t hear, trading sugars and warnings through vast underground networks while we walk above them, oblivious, thinking ourselves the main characters.

I wonder what future humans will romanticize about our era. Will they miss the smell of rain on hot asphalt? The particular texture of turning a physical book page? The small rebellion of choosing to walk instead of being carried by machines?

Sometimes I leave my phone at home just to remember what it feels like to be unreachable. To let thoughts stretch without interruption. The mind is a wild garden—neglected, it grows strange and beautiful things. Given space, it will surprise you.

There’s a quiet courage in staying curious. In refusing to let the world make you smaller or more cynical. Every day offers a thousand tiny doors. Most we never notice. But some—some swing open when we least expect them, revealing rooms inside ourselves we never knew existed.

(Word count: 248)
